title: MQTT QoS 1 telemetry with reconnect and backoff
objective: Publish at least one QoS 1 telemetry payload to a localhost MQTT broker, document ClientId and session choice, and demonstrate a forced disconnect with a listed backoff and a retried or duplicate-explained in-flight message.
whyThisMatters: Edge nodes drop off Wi-Fi and cellular. QoS 1 without a reconnect story is QoS 0 with extra packets. This task uses the OASIS MQTT 5.0 spec and a broker you run yourself — never a paid cloud IoT hub.
evidence: A localhost broker config or run command (Eclipse Mosquitto or equivalent) committed or captured; no cloud endpoint in the config
Client sources or a documented Paho/libmosquitto program plus a thin wrapper you wrote
A captured subscriber or broker log showing the QoS 1 payload received
SESSION.md stating ClientId and clean-start versus persistent-session choice with one sentence of reason
A captured reconnect run listing backoff delays and showing the in-flight message retried or a duplicate explained by packet identifier
Reflection notes answering the task questions
acceptanceCriteria: The broker listens on localhost (or a documented loopback address); the client config contains no public cloud IoT hostname.
A QoS 1 PUBLISH is received by a subscriber; the captured log shows the topic and payload.
SESSION.md states the ClientId string and whether Clean Start (MQTT 5) / clean session is true or false, with one sentence of reason.

A forced disconnect mid-flight is followed by reconnect delays that match a list of at least two backoff values written in SESSION.md, and the in-flight payload is either retried or a duplicate is explained by a packet identifier in the log.
